title: Chapter 46 — The Property Manager
intro: The volume buyer — unit turns, the standard-unit program, and frictionless portfolio service.

sections.title: The Property Manager Mindset
sections.content:
Property managers are volume buyers with simple requirements. They need reliable, affordable appliances that can be replaced quickly when they fail. They need consistent pricing across their portfolio. They need delivery coordinated with tenant schedules. And they need warranty service handled without involving the tenant more than necessary.

This is not a design conversation. This is a logistics and value conversation.

sections.title: The Standard Unit Program
sections.content:
Create a standard appliance package at two or three price tiers. Budget tier for basic units, mid-range for upgraded properties. Standardize the models so every unit in a building gets the same fridge, range, and dishwasher. This simplifies ordering, delivery, and service.

Offer portfolio pricing — a flat discount for the annual volume commitment. Even 5-8 percent off on a 50-unit annual volume is meaningful for the property manager and the consistent revenue is valuable for you.

sections.title: Frictionless Service
sections.content:
Property managers hate friction. Create a reorder system where they can text you 'unit 4B needs a fridge, same as last time' and you handle everything — quote, order, delivery scheduling with the tenant, haul-away, and installation.

The property manager who has to call three times to get a fridge replaced will find someone easier to work with. The one who sends a text and gets a confirmation back in an hour will never leave.
